name: sms-send
description: Send an SMS text message to a person via the office Telnyx DID. recipient takes a contact ID, or "principal" for the principal; you choose the person and the number comes from their verified SMS identity. A #label (principal#personal) is a hint for which labelled identity, not a phone number. Someone with no contact record must be recorded first with contact-create; a phone number here is refused. 1:1 only (no groups/MMS in v1). If Telnyx returns a carrier STOP (error 40300), treat the recipient as opted out and record a contact KG fact — do not retry.

inputs.recipient: string (contact ID or "principal", optional #label hint such as principal#personal — a hint, not a phone number. For someone with no contact record, contact-create first)
inputs.context_bridge: string? (JSON — optional context bridge registration that adds a delegation hint so the agent can route any reply faster. Tracking is automatic but best-effort even without it: registration happens after the send and can fail, and what it registers expires — unless you set expires_in_hours, about 24 hours when this parameter is usable and about 6 hours when it is absent or unusable (on a task-wake turn, about 7 days either way). Unusable means invalid JSON, not an object, or no agent_id: the whole bridge is dropped without telling you and the send gets the 6-hour window, so a typo here costs the longer window. An invalid optional field (e.g. an expires_in_hours that is not a positive number) is dropped on its own, also without telling you, and the rest of the bridge still registers. A valid expires_in_hours replaces that default outright, in either direction: a smaller number gives a shorter window, not a longer one (a deployment may configure different defaults). Set expires_in_hours whenever the reply may land after that — anything the recipient will answer after a night, a weekend, or a trip. Err on the longer side: a stale entry costs a little noise, while an expired one loses the thread. If the entry expired or was never registered, the reply arrives as an unrecognised cold inbound. Shape: {agent_id, expected_reply?, delegation_hint?, metadata?, expires_in_hours?}. delegation_hint must be the agent id of the specialist that owns the reply (e.g. calendar); a hint naming no registered specialist is dropped. Example: {"agent_id":"coordinator","delegation_hint":"calendar","expected_reply":"confirmation or reschedule request"})

outputs.recipient_identity: string? (label of the number used for a reference, or "primary" or "unlabelled")
